summary.prose: Building this fix means changing the install decision in the two update paths (the TypeScript update service and the daemon-ctl.sh script) to a marker written only after a successful install, adding the C++17 compiler flag to every daemon npm install including the installers, and proving it with fake-npm tests over a scratch git checkout plus a real clean install and a real update of the installed daemon.

tasks.title: maintenance.update installs on a missing or stale marker, with C++17 CXXFLAGS
tasks.summary: In update() (src/cli/services/maintenance.ts), replace the lockfile-changed decision with the install-marker rule: read node_modules/.insrc-install-ok, compare it with the synced lockfile's git blob hash, remove the marker before an install, write it after npm install exits 0, and run npm install with CXXFLAGS extended by -std=c++17. Keep skipInstall, the failure result and the lockfile-churn discard. Add the fake-npm integration test over a scratch git checkout.
acceptanceChecks: An update after a failed install installs again, and the marker exists only after a successful install
A matching marker skips the install and the log says the marker matches the lockfile; a stale or missing marker installs
npm sees CXXFLAGS ending in -std=c++17 with any existing CXXFLAGS kept
skipInstall leaves npm uncalled and the marker unchanged; a failed install returns { ok:false, error:'npm install failed' }
An empty lockfile hash installs and writes no marker; a marker write failure returns ok:false

tests.name: S001 t1: an update after a failed install installs again, and the marker exists only after a successful install
S001 t1: a matching marker skips the install; a stale or missing marker installs
S001 t1: npm runs with -std=c++17 appended to the caller's CXXFLAGS
S001 t1: skipInstall leaves npm uncalled and the marker unchanged
S001 t1: an empty lockfile hash installs and writes no marker; a marker write failure fails the update

tasks.title: daemon-ctl.sh applies the same marker rule and CXXFLAGS
tasks.summary: In scripts/daemon-ctl.sh, npm_install_if_needed uses the same marker path, content and decision as t1, removes it before and writes it after a successful install, and runs npm install with CXXFLAGS extended by -std=c++17; SYNC_LOCK_HASH_BEFORE no longer drives the decision. Add an integration test driving `daemon-ctl.sh update --skip-build` over a scratch checkout with a fake npm.
acceptanceChecks: The failed-then-retried, matching, stale and missing marker cases behave as in t1
npm sees CXXFLAGS ending in -std=c++17 with an existing value kept
An empty lockfile hash installs and writes no marker
A marker written by update() is honoured by daemon-ctl.sh and the other way round
--skip-install leaves npm uncalled; a failed install exits 4

S001 t2: daemon-ctl.sh installs on a stale or missing marker, with -std=c++17 appended to CXXFLAGS
S001 t2: daemon-ctl.sh and maintenance.update honour each other's marker
S001 t2: --skip-install leaves npm uncalled; an empty lockfile hash installs and writes no marker

tasks.title: Installers build with C++17 and write the install marker
tasks.summary: In scripts/insrc-daemon-install.sh, run npm install with CXXFLAGS extended by -std=c++17 and, after it succeeds, write the marker holding `git hash-object package-lock.json` of the checkout; copy the result to vscode-plugin/assets/insrc-daemon-install.sh. Extend src/config/__tests__/installer-defs.test.ts.
acceptanceChecks: Both installer copies set CXXFLAGS with -std=c++17 on the npm install
Both write the marker after the install, holding the checkout's lockfile blob hash, so the first update after a fresh install skips

tests.name: S001 t3: the installer builds with -std=c++17 and writes the install marker after npm install, in both identical copies

tasks.title: Real install and installed-daemon update smoke, then the full sweep
tasks.summary: Clean clone of the repository under Node 22: npm install through the new path builds every native module including fs-ext and the project-memory native probe loads; after the push, update the installed daemon (~/.insrc/daemon): it installs once (no marker yet) and skips on the next update. Record both as evidence, then run the full test sweep once.

Full sweep recorded with every failure classified
